caseno: Appeal from Original Order (FMA) No. 272 of 2002
lawyer:
Ramzan Ali Sikder with Md Motahar Hossain Advocates------ For the Appellant. 
AQM Fazlul Haque Khan with Jannatul Akhter, Advocates------ For the Respondents.
parties:
KLM Royal Dutch Airlines ------ Appellant.
Vs.
Travelscene Ltd & another------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
SAN Mominur Rahman J : This appeal arises out of the judgment and order dated 15-11-2000 passed in Title Suit No. 51 of 1994 by the Subordinate Judge 3rd Court making the award dated 22-11-93 for Taka 50,45,932 given by the Arbitral Tribunal in Arbitration Case No. 1 of 1992, a Rule of the Court. 

 2. The respondent Travelscene Ltd, as first party, initiated the arbitration claiming an amount of Taka 12,86,16,100 against KLM Royal Dutch Air- lines, the Second Party, as compensation for termination of the General Sales Agency (GSA) as per clause-18 of the GSA Agreement contending, amongst others, that the first party was appointed as General Sales Agent of the second party in terms of agreement, which became effective from March 15, 1986 and has been terminated in terms of clause 18(1) of the GSA Agreement by a notice dated 10-1-92 with effect from 12-3-92, and as per said termination the first party returned all papers and documents of the second party and also submitted the relevant accounts with which there is no dispute. However, in terms of clause 18( 1) of the GSA agreement the first party initiated the arbitration proceeding through Court, the Arbitral Tribunal being appointed with consent of the parties and the second party participated in the arbitration and the Arbitral Tribunal in due course made the award allowing compensation on two heads of accounts and refused other heads of accounts claimed in the affidavit of claims and that the first party as per provisions of the Arbitration Act, 1940 applied to the  Court for making the award a Rule of Court by filing Title Suit No. 51 of 1994 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, and the second party contested the suit and that on consideration of the materials on record and the submissions of the learned Advocates of the contesting parties the learned Subordinate Judge, accepted the award as given by the Arbitral Tribunal declaring the same as a Rule of the Court, rejecting the prayer of the second party for setting aside the award and that thus being aggrieved the second party preferred the instant first miscellaneous appeal. 

 4. The learned Advocate appearing for the second party appellant submitted that the learned Arbitral Tribunal misconducted in awarding Taka 38,13,081 under the head "Opportunity Cost of Directors Investments" since the said amount as claimed is without any basis, no supporting evidence could be produced before the Arbitral Tribunal and that the Arbitral Tribunal without looking for the supporting evidence and without having any materials for being satisfied about the claim made the award for Taka 38,13,081 arbitrarily and whimsically. The learned Advocate further submitted that as the first party claimed that the Directors of the first party invested Taka 6,63,000 in the GSA business of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines of the second party and the said amount has reached at Taka 38,13,081 only with the addition of the accrued interest @ 18% and 17% on Taka 6,63,000. The learned Advocate submitted that in support of their claim the first party produced the audited balance sheets for the years 1987 to 1991 and no where in those balance sheets the said loan amount of Taka 6,63,000 of the Director has been shown and thus, when the alleged loan of Taka 6,63,000 has not been proved, the award of Taka 38,13,081 as given is without any basis and cannot be maintained and further addition of interest on the said principal amount of Taka 6,63,000 is ex facie illegal, inasmuch as no private citizen can ask for any interest against any kind of loan facility without having any licence from the prescribed authority as per prevailing laws of Bangladesh. In support of his contention that in allowing the said amount at Taka 38,13,081 the Arbitral Tribunal has misconducted, the learned Advocated referred to a decision of the Indian jurisdiction in connection with section 30 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, which is also a relevant law in the instant case, in the case of Union of India vs Mahta Teja Singh & Co, reported in AIR 1983 Delhi 297, wherein it has been held that the conduct of the arbitrator in making the award allowing the claim without himself looking into the report on which the claim was based and without allowing respondent an opportunity for inspection thereof, amounts to misconduct in the proceeding, resulting in denial of natural justice and thus rendered the award liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate submitted that in the instant case the awarded amount of Taka 38,13,081 has been given without looking into any supporting papers, inasmuch as no supporting papers or documents have been filed in respect of the said claim. The learned Advocate, however, submitted that in the award compensation of two heads of account has been given i.e. one for Taka 12,32,861.76 under the head of "net loss incur- red by the first party during GSA period" and under the second head of account for Taka 38,13,081 being the "Opportunity Cost of Directors Investment made in Travelscene Ltd for KLM, GSA business" and that learned Advocate since could not convince us against the award given for Taka 12,32,861.76 submitted that the portion of the award for Taka 38,13,081 in the circumstances should be set aside. The learned Advocate, in support of his contention, referred to a decision of our Appellate Division in the case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Kibria and Associates Ltd, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 97, and submitted that the Arbitral Tribunal has no authority to award pre reference interest, pointing out to the interest added with the principal amount of Taka 6,63,00 claimed as Opportunity Cost of the Director's Investment in the GSA business transaction. On careful reading of the judgment as well as the relevant law, it appears that the pre-reference interest as mentioned in the case reported in 46 DLR (AD) 97 relates to interest allowed on the award amount for the period prior to the initiation of the arbitration and the said principle is not applicable on the amount, which has already been merged with the principal. The learned Advocate also referred to another decision of the Indian Jurisdiction in the case of KP Poulose vs State of Kerala, reported in AIR 1975 SC 1259, wherein it has been held that the action of the Arbitrator amounts to misconduct when Arbitrator ignores material documents produced and the learned Advocate relying on the said decision submitted that no award can be given without any basis and an Arbitrator must look into all papers and documents produced before it prior to making any award. The learned Advocate submitted relying on the observation made by their Lordships of the said Indian Supreme Court, that under section 30(a) of the Arbitration Act award can be set aside when an Arbitrator has misconducted himself or proceeding. Misconduct is not a connotation of moral lapse. It comprises legal misconduct which is complete if the Arbitrator on the face of the award arrives at an inconsistent conclusion even on his own finding or arrives at a decision by ignoring very material documents, which throw abundant light on the controversy to arrive at a just and fair decision and it is in this sense that Arbitrator has misconducted the proceeding in the case and their Lordships therefore had no hesitation in setting aside such award and that in the facts and circumstances of the case the said decision is applicable in the instant appeal in all respects. 

 5. The learned Advocate submitted that the Court below in deciding the case framed an issue as to whether there was any misconduct, legal or procedural, in the award but the learned Court below, considering the provisions of clause 18(1) of the contract, arrived at his decision to the effect that there was no error of law or misconception of law and hence there was no misconduct. The learned Court below failed to consider the fact that the compensation allowed on the head of "Opportunity Cost of the Director's Investment", for Taka 38,13,081 was not based on or supported by any evidence and therefore, awarding of such amount is a misconduct on the part of the Arbitral Tribunal, inasmuch as the Arbitral Tribunal is not authorised to award any compensation arbitrarily at its wilI or wish. All compensation when allowed must be supported by or based on evidence on record. The learned Advocate submitted that a specific ground was taken by the second party before the Court below to the effect that there is absolutely no basis for entertaining the claim Opportunity Cost of Directors and Share- holders and the same is contrary to all recognised jurisprudence and also amounts to the penalising a party to the contract and that too not for valid reason and the compensation of Taka 38,13,081 was mechanically allowed without proper evidence, but the Court below did not consider the said ground and thereby arrived at a wrong decision in allowing the award in respect of the said claim under the head Opportunity Cost of the Directors Investment. The learned Advocate also submitted that no material is available in the record to show that the alleged amount of Taka 6,63,000 has at all been utilised in GSA business and that the' loan given by the Directors to the company is an independent and a separate transaction, which cannot bind the 3rd party, without proving that such loan amount has been accepted by and used or utilised for the benefit of such 3rd party and that too with the consent of the 3rd party concerned. 

 6. The learned Advocate appearing for the first party respondent submitted that the arbitration proceeding is a special proceeding under a special law, which has been adopted for the purpose of speedy disposal of a dispute arising out of a contract, containing an arbitration clause therein. Relying on the decision in the case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Kibria and Associates Ltd, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 97, the learned Advocate submitted that their Lordships in the said decision relied on the decision in the case of Addams vs Great North to the Scotland Ry reported in (1981) AC 31 to the effect that where the parties have selected their judge in such cases one should have to show a great deal more than a mere error in the conclusion to which he has arrived before the Court can interfere with the award and that the parties have agreed to accept the arbitrator's decision on the question of law as well as the decision upon 'fact and, in that view of the matter, the learned Advocate submitted that it cannot be said in the case that the Arbitral Tribunal has misconducted in awarding the compensation in respect of the head "Opportunity Cost of Director's Investment", inasmuch as the Arbitral Tribunal on detailed discussion found that the directors have invested Taka 6,63,000 in the company, and, as such, the Directors are entitled to get compensation and accordingly, the Tribunal arrived at its decision in awarding Taka 38,13,081 and the parties, under the said arbitration, cannot now challenge the said amount. The learned Advocate relying on the decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Bangladesh Telegraph and Telephone Board vs Lithi Enterprise Ltd, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 63, wherein their Lordships in the Appellate Division have considered that the High Court Division's observation in the case to the effect that misconduct on the part of the arbitrators may be a ground for setting aside the award but the appellant did not take any such plea before the Subordinate Judge, to find any such misconduct submitted that since the appellant did not take any specific ground of misconduct, earlier, now such plea cannot be agitated i.e. the allegation of misconduct for awarding the compensation of the said Taka 38,13,081 cannot be challenged before this Court. The learned Advocate also submitted that because of inordinate delay in disposing of this matter and having regard to the amount of compensation allowed against quantum of the claim made by the first party respondent, interest on the decretal amount may be allowed. 

 7. The learned Advocate for the first party respondent also referred to the case of Asalat Zaman vs Bangladesh, reported in 55 DLR (AD) 139 and submitted that the Court has discretion to award interest on the awarded amount till realisation. 

 9. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions of the learned Advocates of the contesting parties as well as the decisions referred to by the learned Advocates, we are of the view that the learned Advocate for the appellant is now challenging the award of Taka 38,13,081 given as compensation under the head Opportunity Cost of Directors Investment. It appears that the submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellant has substance to the effect that the said award so far it relates to Taka 38,13,081 as given is not supported by any documentary evidence nor has any basis but has been given merely on the basis of the claim as made in the affidavit of claim submitted before the Arbitrate Tribunal. The learned Advocate for the first party respondent could not show us any material available in the case record, that Taka 6,63,000 has been, in fact, invested by the Directors in the GSA business of the second party appellant or utilised the said amount of Taka 6,63,000 in the GSA business of second party-appellant. The award of Taka 38,13,081 also appears to be not proper in view of the decisions cited, particularly the cases reported in AIR 1975 (SC)1259 (KP Poulsoe) and AIR 1983.(Delhi) 297 (Union of India Delhi), 46 DLR (AD) 97, (BADC), wherein their Lordships have held that any award not based on any supporting evidence as well as any award given without considering the materials on record tantamounts to misconduct on the part of the arbitrator(s) and is liable to be set aside. It is also on record that the compensation as awarded for Taka 38,13,081 includes the accrued amount of interest on the alleged principal loan amount of Taka 6,63,000 and as per prevailing laws of Bangladesh, a person without a licence from the prescribed authority is not legally entitled to accept any interest on any loan amount. Further accrued interest as calculated is at the rate of 18% or 17% but there is no supporting material or evidence available in the record to show the basis for adopting such higher rate of interest i.e. @ 17% or 18%. In such view of the matter, we hold that the compensation as awarded for Taka 38,13,081 on the head of "Opportunity Cost of Directors Investment" is without any basis and thus liable to be set aside. It is further to be noted that in the grounds of objection taken before the learned Subordinate Judge; the second party has categorically mentioned that the Tribunal has mechanically allowed the compensation under clauses-A and B without proper evidence and there is no basis for entertaining the claim for Opportunity Cost of Directors and Share-holders and therefore, the objection as raised by the learned Advocate for the second party appellant that such objection cannot be entertained by this Court is against the record. It is true that the second party appellant did not use the word "misconduct" but the ingredients of misconduct in detail have been mentioned in the grounds of objection, but those were not considered or discussed by the Court below. 

 11. From the averments made in the pleadings and the contents of the judgment of the Court below, it appears that the Court below confirmed the award allowing the compensation holding that there was no breach of contract and the contract has been cancelled in accordance with the terms of the contract and that the clause 18(1) of the Contract provides for compensation in case of termination of the contract by the second party-appellant. The contract was not for any definite period and admittedly the first party respondent had to make investments for the second party's GSA business and it is on record that a new office was taken on rent and carried on the GSA business for the period 1986 till termination and that the materials on record show that the business expanded during this period and the contract was not cancelled either on the ground that the second party will not carry on its business further or that the second party itself will carry on the business and that the first party made the investment with its legitimate expectation to carry on the business until the contract is terminated for any breach of the contract on its part, and it is on record that the second party after terminating the contract has given the said GSA business to another business firm, and thus both on equity and on law apart from clause 18(1) of the GSA Agreement the first party is entitled to get compensation for being deprived from profit for a reasonable period and accordingly, the first party prayed for compensation for such deprivation, and though due note of which was taken by the arbitrators but no award has been given on such account and the first party also did not move the Court below against non-awarding of compensation on such account. 

 13. The right to claim compensation by the first party is given by said clause-18( 1) in case of termination of GSA Agreement by the second party when such termination is not based on any breach of conditions of the contract or for any valid reason and the claim for compensation by the first party apart from being in accordance with the terms and conditions is also supported by the principle of natural justice. 

 14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the submission of the learned Advocate and decisions of cases referred to we are of the view that the appellant has succeeded in part in the appeal.
